clue.text: Say one's in since getting protection

clue.text: Swimmer's spirit largely bolstered by support

explanation.surface: Seagulls sound like cats when they call, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Mew is an old word for a gull, so 'Seagulls' is the definition, not part of the cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mew, or sea mew, is a gull, so the plural names seagulls.

clue.text: Giving ammunition to a Republican dynasty

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China

explanation.surface: A political party is supplying weapons to a ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm someone is to supply them with weapons, here figuratively giving them ammunition.

clue.text: Don Juan's second wild affair bears unwanted child

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the second letter of the name Juan

clue.text: Got rid of some lines and made less

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as DE-CREASED, ironed out, rather than the usual word for reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means reduced in its ordinary sense and, split as de-creased, means smoothed of wrinkles.

clue.text: Prepare for success, perhaps having space by top of garden

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word garden is used

clue.text: Stymie sailors reportedly supporting veto

explanation.walkthrough: Banjax is Irish slang, popular in Britain, for ruin or thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To banjax something is to wreck or thwart it, which is what stymie means.

clue.text: The man's offspring half-heartedly expressed disapproval

parts.note: his is the possessive for a man

indicators.note: one of the two letters at the heart of the word is lost

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: To hiss is to make a sibilant sound of disapproval, as an audience does at a villain.

clue.text: Stops prescribed drugs with nothing in

parts.note: statins are drugs prescribed to lower cholesterol
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Stations are stopping places, such as railway stations where trains halt.

clue.text: Supply small amount of money to get boost

parts.note: to fill is to supply, as in filling an order
1p, one penny, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Providing a little cash to give someone a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 1p is one penny in British money; the figure 1 becomes the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or lift, something that gives a boost.

clue.text: Experimental patch used to cover eye in speech

parts.note: the letter I sounds the same

clue.text: Gelded, oddly, by prison doctor

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth letters of the word Gelded are taken

explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a person beside the prison; it is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To juggle figures or accounts is to manipulate them dishonestly, as doctoring them does.

clue.text: A sign of life possibly from British, suppressing each obsession

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece presses down on those below it

parts.note: a thing, as in 'having a thing about', is an obsession

explanation.surface: A British reserve that holds down every passion might still show some sign of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing is one of the basic indications that a person is alive.

clue.text: Sort of basket game adopted by the Greeks initially

indicators.note: the game letters are taken in by the others
the first letters of the and Greeks

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: A kind of basket-weaving game was taken up by the ancient Greeks.
explanation.walkthrough: A trug is a shallow wooden garden basket, a British gardening staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A trug is a shallow oblong basket, traditionally used by gardeners.

clue.text: Twist as priest featuring in Hard Times

indicators.note: the priest appears inside the other letters

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
X is the multiplication sign, times

clue.text: Minor setback which exposed copper on top of perjury

explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal; 'exposed' strips the word which to HIC.

clue.text: Status of Conservative dismissed by eccentric

indicators.note: the letter is sent away from the word

parts.note: a crank is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: A Conservative's standing was rubbished by an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank is one's position or standing in a hierarchy, i.e. status.

clue.text: River rising fast is evocative

parts.note: the Oder is a river of Central Europe
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A river rising quickly calls up memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like an adverb about the rising river; it is the noun, a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent of something means strongly suggestive or reminiscent of it.

clue.text: Staple food may see a strike backed by millions…

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million

indicators.note: the words are read back to front

parts.note: to strike coins is to coin them

explanation.surface: A walkout over basic food may be supported by millions of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue, but this clue stands alone; 'strike' means to mint, not a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: Manioc is cassava, a starchy root that is a staple diet in much of the tropics.

clue.text: Effect of international legislation harbouring politician

parts.note: an act is a piece of legislation
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The effect of international law with a politician tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is the influence or effect something has.

clue.text: …in effort to incorporate objective

indicators.note: the effort word takes the objective inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt or effort

clue.text: Coarse — and enthusiastic seeing husband put down

clue.text: State of currency keeping me in

clue.text: Fare cut the old American rejected?
